DryRunAuth.description:
The `auth` object of a dry-run envelope: the credential a request would go
out under.

app.description:
The app whose stored credential would be sent. Absent for a bearer
token the environment supplies, which belongs to no stored app.

token_expired.description:
Whether the `OAuth2` login's token has expired. An expired token is
reported, not refreshed.

username.description: The `OAuth2` login, the one credential with a user name.

NextAction.description:
What the caller should do next. Closed set; agents branch on it.

A newer release can add a member, so a caller treats one it does not
recognize as its default branch.

oneOf.description: No app carries client credentials; register one.
The target app has credentials and no token; sign in.
Another app is the one to use; rerun naming it.
The store could not be read or parsed; look at the file.
X refused the app; enroll it in the developer portal.

The invocation was not one the tool takes, a word that names no
command or a usage error; read the help it names.

The wait on an upload's processing ended before X reported a final
state, and the upload is intact; wait on the same media id again.

X rate limited the request and said when the window resets; send it
again once that time has passed.
Nothing is wrong with the request; send it again.

The input, or the local state the command read, is what failed, and
no other command repairs it; change it before another try.
The tool or the library is at fault; report it.

The command destroys something and ran without its confirmation;
run it again with the flag that confirms it.
One other command repairs this; run it.

NextStep.description:
The `next_step` object carried by an error envelope.

At most one of [`Self::command`] and [`Self::template`] is present: a
command is a verbatim invocation safe for a non-TTY caller, while a
template is one the caller finishes or decides on before running it. It
carries angle-bracket placeholders to fill in; under
[`NextAction::Confirm`], the invocation that destroys once it runs; or,
after a 401 or a 429 with no reset on the status read after `xr media
upload`, the resumed wait to run once the credential works or the window
passes. A step with neither names an action
that is not an `xr` invocation, with `docs` when a page covers it:
[`NextAction::EnrollApp`], [`NextAction::WaitAndRetry`] except on that
status read, [`NextAction::Retry`], [`NextAction::FixInput`],
[`NextAction::ReportIssue`], and [`NextAction::InspectStore`] when the
command that failed is the one that reports on the store. Five
[`NextAction::FixInput`] steps carry an invocation:
[`Self::listen_on_free_port`], [`Self::fix_input_with`],
[`Self::fix_input_template`], [`Self::step_two_again`], and the one
[`resume_after_upload_hint`] gives a 401.

command.description: A runnable invocation, when one exists.

docs.description: Documentation URL, when a recipe exists.

template.description: An invocation the caller finishes or decides on before running it.

Warning.description:
A diagnostic the library raised during a run, as a structured document
carries it. It did not end the run: a failure is the envelope itself.

message.description:
What the library reported, in its own words. The wording is not
contract; branch on `target`.

target.description: The part of `xr` that raised it, such as `xdk::config` or `xdk::store`.

description: The three envelope variants — one per `status` discriminator value.

oneOf.description:
Success envelope. `payload` holds verb-specific fields; agents
merge them flat at the top level for legibility.

warnings.description:
What the library warned about during the run, on the document a
successful run writes on stderr when a warning fired. Stdout's
document never carries it.

oneOf.description:
Dry-run envelope. Its body declares the keys that are the envelope's
own; any other key is one of the command's inputs. Boxed like the
error body, for its size.

app.description: The active app name, on the same refusal.

auth.description:
The credential the request would go out under, read offline. Absent
on a refusal, and on a command that sends no request.

available_in_app.description: Auth schemes available for the active app, on the same refusal.

command.description: The command the answer is about. A raw request carries none.

confirmation_required.description:
Present and `true` on a destructive command whose real run would stop
to ask. Absent under `--force`, where nothing would stop.

endpoint.description:
Endpoint template the request would target, when no stored scheme
serves it.

exit_code.description: Exit code the verb would have returned on actual execution.

message.description: The message the real run's error would carry.

method.description:
HTTP method the request would use, on the same refusal or a raw
request.

next_step.description:
The step the real run's error would carry; one that reruns the
invocation keeps `--dry-run`.

other_apps_with_creds.description: Other apps holding credentials, when the active one holds none.

reason.description: Why the real run would fail, when it would: the `reason` of its error.

requested.description:
Auth scheme the caller asked for, on the same refusal; `null` when
auto-detect ran.

response_schema.description:
The `xr schema` invocation that describes the command's response,
on a command with a typed response. A raw request carries none.

rule.description: The input rule the real run would refuse, under `validation`.

supported.description: Auth schemes the endpoint accepts, on the same refusal.

value.description: The offending input, as it was given, when the broken `rule` names one.

would_succeed.description: True iff every precondition checked clean.

oneOf.description:
Error envelope. Every field the runtime emits is declared on
[`ErrorBody`], so an undeclared key cannot reach a caller. Boxed
because that body is much larger than the success variant.

account.description:
The handle, without its `@`, a lookup found no account for, under
`not-found`: the first such handle when the lookup named several.

action.description: Skill verb the envelope reports on.

available_in_app.description: Auth schemes available for the active app.

backtrace.description:
The stack at a panic, as Rust prints it; present on the `internal`
error a panic answers with when `RUST_BACKTRACE` asks for one.

bearer.description: Whether `auth clear` targeted the bearer token.

command_preview.description: The `git clone` a skill verb would run, its hardening flags omitted.

destination_status.description:
What a skill verb found at `install_dir` before it cloned: `absent`,
`empty-dir`, `non-empty-dir`, or `file`.

exit_code.description:
Structured exit code per the sysexits-inspired matrix in
`xurl::error`.

host.description: Agent host a skill verb targeted.

install_dir.description: Directory a skill verb would install into.

installations.description:
One report per host on a skill verb's `--all` run. The top-level
`reason` and `next_step` speak for the host with the worst exit code.

known_properties.description: Property names at the last node an `xr schema --path` resolved.

legacy_install_dir.description:
A copy of the skill bundle at a location the host still reads but `xr`
does not install to.

media_id.description:
Media id whose processing a wait gave up on, under
`processing-timeout`, where the upload is intact; or the one X
refused after processing it, under `invalid-request`. `media upload`
carries it on any error that ends its wait, since the upload finished
and stdout holds no result.

message.description: Human-readable message. Omitted entirely (not `null`) when absent.

method.description: HTTP method the request would have used.

name.description: App name a destructive verb targeted.

next_step.description:
What the caller should do next, when a recovery step exists.

`action` is closed: `register-app`, `sign-in`, `select-app`,
`inspect-store`, `enroll-app`, `show-help`, `resume-wait`,
`wait-and-retry`, `retry`, `fix-input`, `report-issue`, `confirm`,
`run-command`. A newer release can add an action, so treat one you
do not recognize as your default branch. A step carries either a
`command`, runnable verbatim by a non-TTY caller, or a `template`
the caller finishes or decides on first, never both: a template
holds angle-bracket placeholders only the caller can fill; under
`confirm`, the invocation that destroys once it runs; or, after a
401 or a 429 with no reset on the status read after `xr media
upload`, the resumed wait to run once the credential works or the
window passes. One whose recovery is not an `xr`
invocation carries neither, and `docs` when a page covers it:
`enroll-app`, `wait-and-retry`, `retry`, `fix-input`,
`report-issue`, and `inspect-store` when a store command is what
failed. After `xr media upload` finished, a `wait-and-retry` on the
status read carries the resumed wait: a command that waits out the
reset X named under `--wait-on-rate-limit`, or a template when X named
none or the media command was given `-H`. Three `fix-input` steps carry
an invocation:
`listen` again on a free port, under `address-in-use`, and two under
`invalid-args`: the invocation with `-u`, `--auth`, or `-t` moved
after the command word it came before, and the `xr schema`
invocation that works for an old name or a scope word. Six carry a
template: the `xr schema --path` invocation with the segment that
named nothing left as `<property>`, under `invalid-args`, three under
`auth-required`: the command that stores the secret `webhooks
listen` lacks, `auth oauth2 --step 2` again with its redirect URL
left as `<redirect-url>`, and the resumed wait after a 401 on the
status read after `xr media upload`, to run once the credential
works; `resume-wait` when the media command was given `-H`, with each
header's value left as `<value>`; and that `wait-and-retry` when X
named no reset or under `-H`.

oauth2_username.description: The `OAuth2` user `auth clear` targeted; `null` when unset.

other_apps_with_creds.description: Other apps holding credentials, when the active one holds none.

path.description: Dot path an `xr schema --path` invocation named.

post_id.description: Post id a destructive verb targeted.

reason.description:
Typed kebab-case kind; agents pattern-match on this.

The runtime emits: `auth-required`, `auth-method-mismatch`,
`client-credentials-missing`, `rate-limited`, `not-found`, `forbidden`,
`invalid-request`, `server-error`, `api-error`, `network-error`,
`invalid-args`, `unknown-command`, `invalid-method`,
`invalid-url`, `invalid-path-param`, `validation`, `serialization`,
`io`, `address-in-use`, `token-store`, `internal`, `processing-timeout`,
`confirmation-required`, `no-tty`, `unsupported-pagination`, and the
verb-local `invalid-json`, `unknown-schema`, `validation-failed`,
`missing-host`, `home-not-set`, `destination-not-empty`,
`destination-is-file`, `git-not-found`, `git-clone-failed`,
`not-installed`, and `remove-failed`. The set is closed, and a newer
release can add to it: treat a value you do not recognize as your
default branch.

refused_dir.description:
Directory `skill update` refused to replace, because it holds
something other than the bundle.

rendered_url.description: Endpoint path with path parameters substituted.

requested.description: Auth scheme the caller asked for; `null` when auto-detect ran.

retry_after_secs.description:
Seconds until the rate limit resets, zero once it has; present on a
`rate-limited` error whose own response named the reset.

retry_at.description:
The same reset as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp, for a caller that
schedules the retry instead of sleeping.

rule.description:
The input rule a `validation` refusal broke, as the validator's
kebab-case code (`invalid-username`, `no-list-changes`, ...);
`message` is the sentence for it. Present under `validation`, and on
a dry run that refuses its input.

suggestion.description:
The nearest real command, when one is within the threshold, or the
command that replaced a retired word.

value.description:
The offending input, as it was given, when the broken `rule` names
one: an app name, a redirect URI, a header's position among the `-H`
headers (counted from 1), the seconds a checkpoint runs ahead. Always
a string; a number goes in as its decimal digits.

warnings.description:
What the library warned about before the run failed, each distinct
warning once. Omitted when none fired.

would_succeed.description: Whether a dry-run skill verb would have succeeded.

title: Envelope
